title: Null distance on cosmological spacetimes and monotone convergence
summary: The metric theory of spacetimes studies Lorentzian manifolds using tools of metric geometry. This is achieved via the null distance, which is a definite distance constructed from a time function on a spacetime. This enables the study of Gromov-Hausdorff-type convergence of spacetimes, a program recently initiated by Sakovich and Sormani. In this paper we study such notions of convergence for cosmological spacetimes with compact slices, i.e., $(a,b)\times M$ endowed with a Lorentzian metric $-dt^2+h_t$, where $h_t$ is a family of Riemannian metrics on the compact manifold $M$.
